subject: Composable vs Monolithic: recommendation and decision heuristics
messages:
From: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@medicove.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Packaging question — composable vs single-plan

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here — quick high level question as we prep for IT and finance: we currently can't decide between a composable approach (buy credits/modules a la carte) versus a single monolithic enterprise plan (predictable commit, all features included).

Key constraints for us: predictable monthly spend for budgeting, ability to burst for spikes (teletriage events), and strict audit/compliance for PHI. We also care about seat pooling vs per-endpoint billing.

Can you outline the pros/cons and any middle-ground packaging you've offered to others? Also curious about typical discount thresholds for a 12–18 month commitment and whether upgrades/downgrades mid-contract are practical.

Appreciate a short recommendation we can show to leadership.

—Samuel
Samuel Ortiz
Director, Procurement
MediCove Health

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@medicove.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question — composable vs single-plan

Sam — thanks for the clear constraints. Attaching a small decision matrix and a visual decision tree (redwood-pricing-scenarios.xlsx, decision-tree-deploy.png) — quick summary below. Happy to walk through on a 30m call.

Short recommendation (TL;DR):
- For strict budgeting and procurement simplicity: recommend monolithic reserved plan (annual commit) + burst bucket. Locks price and simplifies billing.
- For rapid feature experimentation and granular cost control: composable modules + pay-as-you-go credits. Better for uncertain usage patterns.
- Middle ground we often propose: Core reserved plan (covers steady-state throughput + seats) + optional module credits for high-variance endpoints. This gives predictability while limiting overcommit.

Practical notes on upgrades/downgrades:
- Upgrades are straightforward (increase commit or add credits) — immediate provisioning.
- Downgrades are possible at renewal; for mid-term reductions we recommend a 30–60 day notice with prorated adjustments unless it's an enterprise contract with custom rollback terms.

Discount thresholds (rough benchmarks):
- Annual commit >= $250k: ~15–20% list discount + 6 months price lock
- Annual commit >= $750k: ~22–30% + extended SLAs / faster support response
- Multi-year or strategic pilots: bespoke credits + onboarding package

Next steps: if you want, I can propose two named packaging options with pricing and a pilot cadence for leadership to review. When's a good time to sync?

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Kimberly, Evelyn, Karthik — looping you in. MediCove (Procurement) asked for a short recommendation; they care about predictable spend, burst capacity, and PHI/audit controls.

Please see my TL;DR above and the attached decision matrix. Need your POV on two things before I send the formal options:
1) Discount guidance / thresholds we can cite for a 12-month commit at $200–500k ARR.
2) A compact hybrid product construct we can offer that has: core reserved capacity (seats + baseline throughput) + optional module credits for experimental endpoints. Can we support seat pooling for this construct?

Goal: produce two named options ("Predictable Core" and "Elastic Modules") with a short pros/cons and a recommended shortlist for procurement.

Short answers and a recommended template:

Discount guidance (12-months):
- $200k–$499k annual commit: 12%–18% off list, with a 3–6 month price lock.
- $500k–$999k annual commit: 18%–25% off list + 30% onboarding credit for first quarter.
- If they can commit to a named pilot and reference (case study), add 5–8% promotional credit.

Product constructs:
1) Predictable Core (recommended for MediCove) — monolithic reserved plan
   - Baseline: seats + reserved GPU capacity sized to steady-state throughput
   - Burst: prepaid burst bucket (metered consumption) that kicks in beyond reserved capacity
   - Billing: single invoice, monthly amortized commit, clear overage thresholds
   - Pros: budget-friendly, simple procurement, easier SOC2/PHI attestation path
   - Cons: potential waste if usage is highly variable

2) Elastic Modules — composable approach
   - Baseline: small reserved seat count + PAYG module credits for new endpoints
   - Billing: credits + metered usage; recommend monthly spend cap to prevent surprises
   - Pros: flexible, low initial commit, good for experimental teams
   - Cons: harder to forecast; procurement may push back on variable billing

3) Hybrid Starter (compromise)
   - Core reserved plan covering core product lines + an "experiment" pool of module credits (quarterly top-up)
   - Seat pooling supported: yes — seats can be pooled across product owners on the same contract (we'll need named seat limits)

Operational notes from Product (Evelyn / Karthik):
- Evelyn: hybrid is the safest; recommend a 3-month pilot with defined SLIs and a cap on module spend.
- Karthik: technical note — if they need end-to-end PHI handling in private deployment we should map to Redwood Private; that has different pricing (platform fee + infra).

I'll draft the two named options and suggested wording for Procurement. Mateo — want me to include the discount table above in the procurement-facing doc?

—Kimberly

Subject: Recommended packaging options for MediCove (two paths + next steps)

Sam — thanks for the patience. Based on your constraints and a quick internal alignment, here are two concrete, procurement-friendly options we recommend. I attached the pricing scenarios and a decision tree.

Option A — "Predictable Core" (Recommended)
- 12-month annual commit: $320,000
- Discount: 16% off list (as quoted)
- Deliverables: reserved capacity sized for steady-state, 250k-token burst bucket pre-purchased for spikes, seat pooling across internal teams (up to 50 named users)
- Compliance: SOC2 + optional Private control plane add-on for PHI (additional platform fee)
- Change window: upgrades immediate; downgrades at renewal or with 60-day notice and prorated true-up

Option B — "Elastic Modules" (Experiment + scale)
- 12-month annual commit: $120,000 + module credits (50k credits)
- Discount: 12% off list on committed portion; credits priced at catalog rate for usage beyond the pool
- Deliverables: small reserved seat pool + credits for experimental endpoints; monthly spend cap option available

Pilot suggestion: 6–8 week pilot on Option A with a reduced commit ($50k) that converts into credit toward a 12-month contract. This gives leadership budget guardrails and lets engineering validate latency/throughput.

If you approve, I'll:
- Send a procurement-ready one-pager with the pricing table and cancellation/upgrade terms.
- Book a 30m call with your finance and IT on Monday to walk the terms.
